note: Shrink-only ceiling on two browser-test anti-patterns. nonWaitingAssertion: a non-waiting isVisible()/isEnabled() result used inside expect(); the timeout option on those calls is IGNORED, so the assertion races rendering. cannotFail: expect(... || true), which passes whatever the page does. Regenerate ONLY with --write-baseline, and only on genuine improvement. Never hand-edit.

paydown.what: Converted non-waiting snapshots to waiting assertions and removed decorative expect(x || true). Both changes are strictly MORE tolerant than what they replaced: a waiting assertion allows time where the snapshot raced the render, and deleting an always-true assertion cannot newly fail. Two assertions were tightened into REAL checks instead of deleted: the federated provenance/origin badges (the subject of their own tests) and the admin users pagination metadata (verified against AdminUsersController::index + respondWithPaginatedCollection before asserting). One was replaced rather than kept: admin pagination presence is genuinely data-dependent, so the test now asserts the user list rendered instead of pretending to check pagination.
